messages:
Marta: ok folks — quick sync. Customer asks are piling up for more granular cost breakdowns, a simple tracing hook pattern, and an error analytics slice. We need a decision on minimum surface for the next sprint.
Sam: +1. we should prioritize a per-route token-cost view and a lightweight trace sampler. customers keep asking for 'why did this request cost X tokens'
Jess: for the cost view: can we wire token-level + model variant + billing tier? even a CSV export would satisfy initial customers.
Liang: sampling: recommend starting with deterministic sampling keys (route + user-tier) and 0.1% baseline. then expose sample rate in UI. avoids config explosion.
Carlos: error analytics: customers want grouped root causes (timeout vs model error vs infra). start with error-code + latency histogram + last-10-outputs. ok?
Marta: that sounds like a good minimum. tradeoffs: more retention costs for storing last outputs, and traces mean more storage & CPU. need launch criteria.
Sam: launch criteria proposal: (1) cost view shows per-route, per-model, per-variant aggregated hourly cost for last 7 days; (2) trace hook can be toggled per-route and records sampled spans with annotations; (3) error analytics surfaces top 5 error buckets and links to sample traces.
Jess: operationally, require rollout: opt-in for 10 pilot customers on hosted API + 2 internal teams on Dedicated. must have feature flags and data export.
Liang: will need tracing hook skeleton in runtime: small header e.g., `X-Redwood-Trace: capture=true` and server-side guard rails to avoid pII capture.
Carlos: about PII — we should include a policy page and sanitize outputs by default (strip >1KB outputs and redact obvious keys). also add explicit checkbox for customer to include full outputs.
Marta: prioritization asks: is this a single epic or split into three (cost, tracing, errors)? splitting helps parallel work but we must keep unified UX.
Sam: split into three epics but same release tag. UX lead can own glue points (common header, exports, queries). devs can land independent APIs.
Jess: timeline idea: 2-week discovery, 3 sprints for implementation, 1 sprint for pilot & fixes. realistic?
Liang: dev estimate: cost-aggregation API + UI = 3 dev-sprints; trace hook runtime + storage + UI = 4 dev-sprints; error analytics = 2 dev-sprints (reusing traces). parallel ok with 6 engineers.
Carlos: risk: cost query pain for historical token accounting if we change model pricing. propose canonical cost-mapper service to normalize model unit costs at ingestion time.
Marta: good call. acceptance criteria to include: accuracy within 5% for aggregated hourly cost vs billing system, trace sampling deterministic, error buckets reproducible.
Sam: customers to invite: AcmeHealth (privacy), ShopFlow (cost sensitivity), NovaSearch (latency). I can coordinate invites.
Jess: one more ask — add an audit log for who toggled tracing and export for compliance. many SOC reviews need that.
Liang: ops-bot note: deploy window for pilot must avoid heavy infra migrations. suggest feature-flag rollout and no infra schema changes in first pass.
ops-bot: reminder: scheduled infra maintenance on 1711113000 — avoid major DB migrations until after. :warning:
Marta: next steps: Sam to draft customer pilot doc, Liang + Sam to mock trace header + sampling config, Jess to draft acceptance matrix, Carlos to prototype sanitizer. I'll collate and schedule a 30m review on Tues.
Sam: I'll ping the customers today.
Jess: drafting acceptance matrix now.
Liang: will drop an initial runtime sketch by EOD.
Carlos: prototyping sanitizer this afternoon.
Marta: thanks — will send calendar invite. :rocket:
